title: Is it already an f32?
starter:
(* true when the double x is exactly representable as a single-precision float.
   NaN and the infinities count as representable. *)
let is_f32 (x : float) : bool =
  false
hints: Round-trip it: squeeze `x` into 32 bits and see if you get the same number back.
`Int32.bits_of_float` rounds to single precision, and `Int32.float_of_bits` turns those bits back into a double.
NaN is never equal to itself, so the round-trip comparison says false for it. Check `Float.is_nan x` separately.

answer.code:
let is_f32 (x : float) : bool =
  Float.is_nan x || Int32.float_of_bits (Int32.bits_of_float x) = x
answer.explain: The reference rounds `x` to f32 and back with `Int32.float_of_bits (Int32.bits_of_float x)` and compares with the original. It special-cases NaN, because `nan = nan` is false even though NaN is representable.
